headline: July PCE 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected, core 3.3% in line; Q2 GDP unrevised at 1.5%
summary: Headline PCE rose 0.2% m/m and 3.7% y/y (June 3.7%, consensus 3.6%); core 0.2% m/m and 3.3% y/y matched. Q2 GDP held at 1.5% annualised with the Q2 core PCE index revised up to 3.6%, durable goods beat at +1.1%, and CME pricing after the data has September at 61% hold / 39% hike with the 10-year at 4.66%.

headline: Iran and Oman agree 7-mile temporary Hormuz corridor; Iran says strait stays shut until US delivers sanctions relief
summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister announced an 11km-wide route through Iranian waters with vessels needing Iranian permission, while insisting Hormuz will not reopen until the June MoU commitments are met; Trump told Al Jazeera he has no timetable for talks and expanded sanctions on 60 entities. WTI is $81.77 (-0.7%) and Brent $86.66 after a 2%+ drop, with EIA crude inventories up only 0.1M barrels vs 1.6M expected.

headline: Canada matches new US 50% tariffs on ~$20B of goods from September 8; Trump says 'time to teach Canada'
summary: After talks collapsed the US imposed 50% duties on about $20B of Canadian imports from August 24; Canada announced dollar-for-dollar 50% tariffs on ~700 US products effective September 8 plus aid for affected firms. Trump told Glenn Beck it is 'time to teach Canada you can't do this anymore'; USD/CAD 1.39, TSX futures -0.1%.

headline: Nvidia options imply a 5.4% move; street wants networking near $17B
summary: Options price a ~$280B swing, below the 6.5% implied in May and the 7.4% 12-quarter average. Networking, ~$15B last quarter, is expected near $17B (+~134% y/y) versus ~100% growth for compute; the stock is $210.56 intraday, -1.2%.

headline: Micron names Bhatia President and COO, DeBoer President and CTPO
summary: Manish Bhatia becomes President and Chief Operating Officer and Scott DeBoer President and Chief Technology and Products Officer, effective immediately; Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana moves to senior advisor to the CEO.

headline: SoftBank weighs $10-20B bond sale to repay its $40B OpenAI bridge loan
summary: Bloomberg says SoftBank is talking to banks about a dollar/euro deal, possibly a 144A, as early as September, to refinance the bridge loan behind its ~$65B OpenAI commitment due by October. SoftBank says nothing is decided; its shares rose 2.8%.

headline: Marvell preview: options imply 10.3%, Q3 bar $3.03B
summary: Consensus for Thursday is $2.72B revenue (+35%) and $0.93 EPS; Benchmark ($275) expects a $3.03B/$1.09 Q3 guide. Options imply a 10.3% move versus ~12% over the last four quarters; consensus target $291.

headline: Taiex +1.5% to 45,833 into Nvidia; TSMC closes NT$2,415 (+0.6%)
summary: Taiwan shares rose 663 points on NT$804B turnover ahead of Nvidia's report; 2330 closed at NT$2,415, up NT$15. Kospi +1.0% with SK hynix +0.6% and Samsung +1.8%.

headline: Meta settles 29-state teen social media trial for up to $16.68B
summary: Meta agreed mid-trial to pay up to $16.68B and adopt default daily time limits for teens, nighttime restrictions, stronger age assurance and expanded parental controls, without admitting wrongdoing. School-district and personal-injury cases continue; shares spiked to $593.34 before settling near $574.

headline: Alibaba completes HK$80B placement of 710M shares; 9988 closes HK$116.60
summary: The placing at HK$112.70 closed with ~60% (HK$47.9B) of net proceeds for global computing infrastructure and ~40% (HK$31.9B) for AI data centres and cloud. Hong Kong shares closed up 2.1% at HK$116.60, 3.5% above the placing price.

headline: AWS to acquire DuckLabs, maker of DuckDB
summary: AWS signed a definitive agreement to buy the Amsterdam-based DuckDB developer for an undisclosed price, closing as soon as next month. DuckDB stays MIT-licensed under the DuckDB Foundation and the co-founders join AWS to fold the engine into its analytics services.

headline: Moonshot AI in talks to have Google, Amazon and Microsoft host Kimi K3
summary: Reuters reports China's Moonshot AI is negotiating revenue-sharing agreements that would let Google Cloud, AWS and Azure host its Kimi K3 model. No dollar figures or timing were disclosed.

headline: Siemens Energy flat on first session after separation news; five brokers reiterate buys
summary: Shares traded EUR 150.76-153.32 and were EUR 151.18 (-1.0%) at 16:29 CEST, in line with a -0.2% DAX, so no sell-the-news move. Deutsche Bank (Buy, EUR 210), Bernstein (Outperform, EUR 210), RBC (Outperform, EUR 200), JPMorgan (Overweight, EUR 245) and Jefferies (Buy) all backed the plan. The unit being separated made EUR 646M profit before special items (+70%) and EUR 686M FCF in FY25 on EUR 5.7B revenue; no buyer, price, brand or timeline yet.

headline: GE Vernova and LS Electric form HVDC joint venture Grid X Technology; shares +1.8%
summary: Signed at CIGRE Paris on Aug 25: the JV will design, manufacture and test voltage-source-converter HVDC equipment (converter transformers first) at LS Electric's Busan base, targeting Korea's West Coast Energy Highway before exporting. Stakes and investment not disclosed. GEV bounced to $943.71 (+1.8%) by 10:38 EDT after a six-session, ~14% slide.

headline: SK hynix +0.6% in Seoul as Kospi hits 6,808; Chinese memory rivals dominate the headlines
summary: Seoul close KRW 1,688,000 (+0.6%, range 1,662,000-1,735,000); ADR flat at $159.29 at 10:37 EDT after a premarket dip on FT/Barron's pieces about YMTC targeting NAND leadership by 2027. Korea Herald says CXMT is close to validating LPDDR6 for Xiaomi's Xring O3 ahead of SK hynix's H2 supply start. Digitimes puts the union's rejection of the wage deal at a 25-vote margin; no new talks scheduled yet.

headline: Bloom's Pelosi rally fades: +3.2% early to $227.34, then $215.32 (-1.0%) by 10:48 EDT
summary: Investing.com attributed the early pop to continued follow-through on the Pelosi disclosure (15,000 shares plus 200 June-2027 $100 calls) and the raised $3.9-4.2B guide; Mizuho is at Outperform, Jefferies Hold ($229), Citi Neutral. The reversal in a flat tape shows how thin the disclosure-driven bid is ahead of Nvidia.

headline: Broadcom -1.0% to $353; options price a 7.3% move on the Sep 2 print
summary: Shares slipped to $353.13 by 10:37 EDT (range $351.12-359.47) into Nvidia. Options imply a 7.3% earnings move; the stock beat the implied move in 3 of the last 8 reports. RBC says Broadcom is set for a beat-and-raise on networking momentum, with TPU share and gross margins the items to watch; BMO ($455, Outperform) wants the $100B FY27 AI revenue target held or raised.

headline: Anthropic to watermark Claude text worldwide for the EU AI Act; Shopify CEO row over AGENTS.md
summary: IT Brief Asia reports future Claude models will carry text watermarks globally at launch because Anthropic cannot yet limit them by region, a compliance step that may unsettle some enterprise users. Separately, Shopify's CEO threatened to drop Claude Code after Anthropic closed a request to support the AGENTS.md agent-instruction standard; Anthropic has since responded (The New Stack, Aug 25). Zoom's earnings also drew attention to its Anthropic stake (a $51M bet now valued at $1-4B).

headline: BYD -1.1% to HK$92.60 two days before interim results; Ulaanbaatar MoU covers EVs, fast charging, storage and SkyShuttle
summary: HK close HK$92.60 (range 91.75-94.10) on no company news ahead of Friday's H1 results. BYD Battery signed a framework MoU with Mongolia's capital on EV adoption, an urban fast-charging network, battery storage and a SkyShuttle transit line; no figures or timeline. Interim results due Aug 28.

headline: Australia July CPI 3.5% vs 3.2-3.3% consensus, trimmed mean steady at 3.6%; RBA September hike odds rise to ~27%
summary: Monthly CPI rose 1.0% m/m (0.8% expected) with trimmed mean 0.5% m/m (0.3% expected), fuel +7.5% in the month and housing +5.0% y/y; the ABS says trimmed mean is unchanged at 3.6%, above the RBA's 3.3% year-end forecast. Markets lifted September hike pricing to 27% from 17% and February 2027 to 80%; AUD/USD rose 0.2% to ~0.7176 while the ASX 200 gave up early gains.

headline: Oil falls a third day on Iran-Oman Hormuz corridor talks; WTI $80.42 (-2.4%), Asia energy stocks slide
summary: Iran and Oman are discussing an interim framework including a temporary navigational corridor and mine clearing for a strait that carried about a fifth of global oil and LNG shipments. Woodside fell more than 4%, Santos ~2%, SK Innovation over 16% and the ASX 200 energy sub-index 2.5%; Brent is $86.41 (-2.5%).

headline: Alibaba HK shares +1.7% to HK$116.10 on placement settlement day, 3% above the HK$112.70 placing price
summary: Hong Kong trading has held above the HK$112.70 placement price with a day range of HK$115.60-117.80 and ~39M shares traded by midday, as the HK$80B placing of 710M shares closes today. Hang Seng +1.0% to 25,757.

headline: Nvidia preview: guide implies ~$91B, consensus $91.7-92.2B and ~$2.08 EPS; guide assumes zero China data-centre revenue, $80B buyback unused
summary: Results land ~6:30am AEST Thursday with the call at 7am AEST. Focus is the Q3 outlook (street ~$104.2B, ~75% gross margin), Blackwell Ultra supply and hyperscaler capex commentary; any China data-centre revenue would be an upside surprise since guidance assumes none. The stock ended a seven-session losing streak on Tuesday, so some optimism is already priced.

headline: Bloomberg: Meta and state AGs have discussed a mid-trial settlement of the teen social media case
summary: Reuters relays a Bloomberg report that Meta and state attorneys general discussed settling in the second week of the Oakland trial; Meta's worst-case estimate is $1.4T of exposure but any deal would be far smaller. Meta has not commented; shares were $567.75 after hours.

headline: Micron CEO Mehrotra sold $38.7M of stock under a 10b5-1 plan
summary: Mehrotra sold 39,994 shares at $959-990 on Aug 21 under a plan adopted Jan 30, retaining 264,503 shares directly and 607,075 via GRATs. Routine, but it lands as the stock sits below its 50-day.

headline: 9fin: Goldman Sachs AM arranging $6.6B GPU-backed private debt for OpenAI with Nvidia backstop
summary: A privately placed $6.6B debt package secured on GPUs and supported by an Nvidia backstop is being put together by GSAM. It is debt, not equity, so it does not move the ~$852B mark, but it adds to Nvidia's customer-financing exposure heading into tonight's call.

headline: SK hynix +1.2% midday Seoul as chipmakers lead Kospi higher into Nvidia
summary: Seoul shares reversed a weak open to KRW 1,698,000 (+1.2%) by 11:20 KST, day range 1,662,000-1,717,000; Kospi +0.9% to 6,804 and Samsung +2.1%. No news yet from the restarted union wage talks; the stock remains ~9% below its 200-day average. ADR last $159.53.

headline: Anthropic sought up to 5GW of AI training capacity in NSW, government emails show
summary: ABC obtained a March 18 Infrastructure NSW email saying Anthropic's CEO wanted to discuss locating up to 5GW of AI training capacity in NSW, possibly outside Sydney; Amodei visited two weeks later. NSW says the figure reflected initial interest and was one of several hyperscale approaches.

headline: BYD's Fangchengbao off-road brand tripled China sales in Jan-Jul as group growth slows
summary: Nikkei reports Fangchengbao sales tripled year on year over January-July while BYD's overall growth slowed, with the brand's first sedan about to launch. A higher-margin sub-brand growing into Friday's interim results.

headline: Intuit drops 7% after hours on FY27 growth guide of 9-10%
summary: Q4 EPS $4.03 and revenue $4.354B both beat, but FY27 revenue growth of 9-10% versus 14% in FY26 and a flat-to-down Mailchimp outlook wiped about $6.9B of value; Zoom fell 3.9% on an in-line revenue guide while Semtech guided Q3 revenue to $405-415M versus $379M consensus.

headline: Iran and Oman propose temporary Hormuz shipping corridor with mine-clearing
summary: A phased framework covers a temporary joint navigation corridor, joint mine-clearing and talks on a permanent corridor, with other Gulf states to be involved; traffic through the strait, which normally carries about a fifth of seaborne oil and LNG, remains largely paralysed, and China condemned the new US sanctions.

headline: Australia July CPI due 11:30 AEST: consensus 3.2-3.3% headline, trimmed mean 3.5%
summary: CBA and ANZ look for 3.2% y/y and NAB and Westpac 3.3%, down from 3.8% on fuel base effects, with the trimmed mean seen easing to about 3.5% from 3.6%; Westpac's 0.4% m/m trimmed-mean call sits slightly above the RBA's track, and an in-line or softer core print would extend the hold at 4.35%.

headline: Google launches Ask Gemini in Google Chat for Workspace customers
summary: From Aug 26 Workspace users can query Gmail, Drive and Calendar, draft updates and generate images from inside Google Chat. Promotional higher usage limits run through Oct 1, 2026, after which usage caps apply. Incremental product depth for Workspace rather than a revenue event.

headline: GE Vernova launches 170 kV SF6-free switchgear at CIGRE Paris
summary: The F35g 170 kV gas-insulated switchgear uses g3 instead of SF6 and completes GE Vernova's SF6-free GIS range from 72.5 to 420 kV. Built in Europe and available for order; no customer orders or volumes disclosed. Product news, not a guidance event.

headline: Google Cloud launches Gemini Enterprise for Legal in preview
summary: Cleary, Freshfields, Weil and Williams & Connolly are launch customers, with connectors to Harvey, iManage, NetDocuments, RelativityOne, Everlaw and Docusign. Second vertical in a day after Financial Services; supports the Cloud growth case.

headline: Mosseri denies suppressing child-safety risks; Instagram design chief admits data was cut from 2023 safety deck
summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri testified in Oakland that he neither encouraged nor knew of any policy to keep negative information from the public. Earlier, product-design director Francesco Fogu acknowledged that data showing teens encountered 1.5x more bullying, suicide, hate, nudity and violent content than adults was removed from a 2023 safety presentation, and that 'take a break' adoption would suffer without being on by default. The 29-state trial runs through September.

headline: Amazon's US apparel share nearly doubles to 17.8% since 2019 as Walmart slips to 6.0%
summary: PYMNTS Intelligence analysis of company revenue against Census clothing sales puts Amazon at 17.8% of US clothing spend in 2026 versus 8.5% in 2019, with apparel sales of $109.4B in 2025 and $55.5B in H1 2026. Walmart's share fell from 7.3% to 6.0% over the same period.

headline: Street looks for $92.2B revenue and a ~$104B Q3 guide as Rubin hand-off and AI financing take centre stage
summary: Consensus for Wednesday's print is $92.18B revenue (nearly double y/y) with Q3 guidance expected near $104.2B (+82.8%) and ~75% gross margin; Morgan Stanley estimates Rubin could add almost $9B of Q3 sales. Nvidia's ~$500B customer financing and $105B OpenAI Ohio lease guarantee are drawing circular-demand scrutiny.

headline: Marvell Q2 preview: Q3 guide vs $3.03B consensus is the swing factor, not the $2.71B Q2 number
summary: Q2 FY27 consensus sits at $2.708B revenue (0.3% above the guide midpoint) and ~$0.93 EPS; the street wants Q3 guidance above $3.03B (+13% q/q) and higher FY27/FY28 targets. Google's 58.97M warrants at $206.58 vest one tranche per $500M of custom-product purchases, 240 tranches through FY2033.

headline: Claude Cowork now shares memory with Claude chat
summary: Anthropic merged the memory system across Claude chat and Cowork, so project context given in one carries into the other. On by default for Free, Pro and Max on web, desktop and mobile; sensitive topics excluded unless users opt in. Same day, Anthropic put up $5M in grants for open-source wellbeing evaluations (applications close Sep 21).

headline: Robinhood closes up 8.2% at $112.09 on crypto rebound and prediction-market note
summary: Bitcoin briefly crossed $81,000 and a Bernstein note pointing to ~$240B of 2026 prediction-market volume (and $1T by 2030) pulled attention to Robinhood, now Kalshi's anchor partner with 1,000+ contracts listed. Volume 9.9M shares, roughly 3x normal.

headline: BYD to launch Sealion 08 flagship SUV on Sep 2, priced 230-280k yuan
summary: Mid-to-large SUV in EV (up to 115 kWh, 900 km CLTC) and PHEV (275-300 km electric-only) forms, second-gen Blade battery and flash charging. The Sealion line did 227,415 units Jan-Jul, 10.2% of group sales. Shares closed HK$93.60 (+0.9%) ahead of Friday's interim results.

headline: Apple Maps ads now showing to users in the US and Canada
summary: Apple confirmed ads began appearing in Maps search results and a new Suggested Places section over the last few days, with delivery ramping to all users in the coming weeks. Ads carry a blue 'Ad' badge; Apple says location and ad data are not tied to the Apple Account. Adds a new services line alongside the M6 Mac mini / M5 Ultra Mac Studio pre-orders (ship Sep 22).

headline: Spotify bundles fandom features into Premium; shares +2.7% to $552.57
summary: SongDNA credits explorer, a weekly Concerts Near You playlist, lyric translation, music videos in the US/Canada, and 'Reserved' (two pre-sale tour tickets held for an artist's top fans, Premium 18+ US/Canada). No new paid tier announced. Spotify says 100M+ subscribers have used SongDNA.

headline: SK hynix wage talks restart from scratch; new union wants cash-only bonus
summary: The tentative deal (6.3% raise, 60% of bonus in shares) failed by 25 votes of 15,045 cast, 93.8% turnout. Korea JoongAng Daily says labor and management return to the table after two months of talks, while a new integrated union formed Aug 13 with 3,400+ members is demanding the old cash-only formula. No strike call yet.

headline: Wall Street closes higher ahead of Nvidia and PCE as oil slides 5% and yields fall
summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.32% to 7,677, the Nasdaq 0.66% to 26,151 and the Dow 0.30% to 53,577 as tech rebounded before Nvidia's Wednesday report; WTI fell 4.9% to $80.65, the 10-year yield dropped to 4.62% and the VIX eased to 15.5. AMD (+4.9%) led on a Raymond James upgrade, Moderna jumped 14%; after hours Intuit fell ~9% on weak guidance while Zoom beat and raised. July PCE and the second Q2 GDP estimate land at 22:30 AEST Wednesday.

headline: Ex-Meta data scientist: only ~0.2% of teens used Instagram's break reminder; Mosseri takes the stand
summary: In the 29-state teen social-media addiction trial in Oakland, former Instagram wellbeing-team data scientist George Volichenko testified under subpoena that roughly two in 1,000 weekly teen users activated the opt-in 'take a break' tool and that leadership rejected making it default because of fear it would dent core engagement metrics; Meta's lawyer countered that 0.2% still meant hundreds of thousands of teens. Instagram head Adam Mosseri began his testimony late Tuesday (Reuters), with the trial expected to run six to eight weeks. META still closed up 2% at $570.05.

headline: Anthropic to pitch IPO investors a $30T+ addressable market on a $65B run-rate, WSJ reports
summary: The WSJ reports Anthropic will tell prospective IPO investors its total addressable market exceeds $30 trillion, topping SpaceX's $28.5T claim, derived from 'the full scope of work that could be completed with AI models'. Q2 revenue was $11.6B, the annualized run-rate reached $65B at end-July and 2028 revenue is projected at $190-200B; an S-1 is expected within weeks for a September/early-October debut at roughly a $2T valuation, potentially raising up to $100B.

headline: OpenAI data-center chief Chris Malone exits, fourth senior departure before planned 2027 IPO
summary: The WSJ reports Chris Malone, OpenAI's head of data centers since March 2025 and a former Meta and Google infrastructure lead, left last week, following Fidji Simo, COO Brad Lightcap and CRO Denise Dresser; the Journal called the cluster of C-suite exits unusual even by pre-IPO standards, while Greg Brockman said 'I'm a constant, Sam is a constant'. Sachin Katti now oversees infrastructure as OpenAI raises projected compute spending to ~$750B through 2030 and signs a 10GW Ohio lease with SB Energy backed by up to $105B of Nvidia guarantees.

headline: Perplexity and Nvidia launch 'Portable Computer', a fully local AI agent for DGX Spark and RTX machines
summary: Perplexity released Portable Computer, an agent platform that runs models, inference and security tooling entirely on local hardware (Nvidia DGX Spark or Linux boxes with 24GB+ RTX GPUs, Windows in September) for Pro, Max and Enterprise subscribers, consuming no billing credits for local work and asking permission before escalating to cloud frontier models. Co-developed with Nvidia, which calls it evidence that 'local AI reached an inflection point', it gives DGX Spark a flagship application; separately Nvidia is reported in talks to invest in Perplexity at a $30B+ valuation.

headline: Morgan Stanley credit desk flags ~$200B of contingent financing exposure from Nvidia's AI ecosystem support
summary: Initiating credit coverage with a neutral view, Morgan Stanley said Nvidia's balance-sheet support for customers via residual-value structures tied to a $500B+ partnership and revenue-sharing deals could reach ~$200B of total credit exposure by end-2028, including ~$170B of contingent and off-balance-sheet obligations, so 'conventional leverage increasingly understates the credit story'; it called the $1T+ of guided GPU/XPU financing the key overhang and told bond investors to be patient despite wider spreads.

headline: Waymo confirms Munich as first EU city, public robotaxi service targeted for late 2027
summary: Waymo said it will begin mapping and manual driving in Munich in the coming weeks with trained specialists behind the wheel, aiming to open fully autonomous ride-hailing to the public toward the end of 2027 in its third market outside the US; the German transport ministry and Bavarian government backed the move, with co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana calling Munich 'a world-class hub for mobility and engineering'.

headline: Rocket Money launches Rowan, an Anthropic-powered AI agent that acts on members' finances
summary: Rocket Companies' Rocket Money unveiled Rowan, an AI agent 'powered by Anthropic' built on a stack of agents trained on Rocket Money data, which monitors finances over text, cancels subscriptions, renegotiates bills and automates savings transfers rather than just surfacing insights; it is available to select subscribers in a new Premium Plus tier with broader rollout later in 2026, a modest new monetization lever for the personal-finance funnel feeding Rocket's mortgage business.

headline: BofA names Nvidia, Marvell and Micron among eight 'enhanced buy' chip stocks despite ~10% SOX downside risk
summary: Vivek Arya told clients semiconductor risk/reward is positive despite three near-term headwinds (macro and data-center backlash, circular-financing concerns, heavy positioning), naming NVDA, MRVL, MU, LRCX, AMD, INTC, ADI and ON; BofA sees ~10% further downside risk to the SOX back to its pre-ChatGPT discount, which it calls unjustified given bullish Q4/Q1 seasonality and a 20x forward multiple against a ~70% earnings CAGR through 2028.

headline: Siemens Energy to separate Transformation of Industry into a standalone company, retain minority stake
summary: In an ad-hoc release at 18:25 UTC, after the Xetra close, Siemens Energy said it is starting preparations for the legal and operational separation of Transformation of Industry (steam turbines, generators, compressors; ~17,000 staff, FY25 revenue EUR 5.7B at an 11.3% margin) into an independent industrial-energy-solutions company. It intends to deconsolidate the unit while keeping a meaningful minority stake, with options ranging from external investors to a capital-markets transaction; Goldman Sachs is running the process and private-equity interest has been reported at a valuation above EUR 10B. No price or timeline was given. Shares closed +2.7% at EUR 152.76 before the release.

headline: OpenAI's Broadcom-co-designed Jalapeno chip claims to beat Nvidia GB300 on inference efficiency
summary: OpenAI published first results for Jalapeno, the 700W inference ASIC it co-developed with Broadcom, claiming up to 1.9x throughput per kilowatt and 3.6x lower latency than Nvidia's 1,400W GB300. It is a public validation of Broadcom's custom-XPU model a week before its Sep 2 report, though Broadcom still closed -0.6% at $356.74 (after-hours $358.00) as the market stays focused on its AI-financing exposure; the claim also raises the bar for Nvidia's Wednesday print.

headline: Sea Limited rallies 6.5% to $123.18 on no company news
summary: Sea closed +6.5% at $123.18, its best day since the Aug 11 Q2 print, with no company-specific announcement; the move tracked a broad EM/Internet bid (MercadoLibre +2.5% to $1,997) and follow-through from post-earnings target hikes at BofA ($143), Barclays ($156), Morgan Stanley ($153) and Benchmark ($175). The stock remains ~36% below its 52-week high with consensus targets near $155.

headline: OpenAI publishes Jalapeño chip benchmarks claiming more throughput per kilowatt than Nvidia Blackwell
summary: OpenAI released first results for its Broadcom-co-designed Jalapeño inference chip: SemiAnalysis's InferenceX benchmark shows more tokens per user and more throughput per kilowatt than current Blackwell systems, per TechCrunch. Hardware lead Richard Ho called it 'a very, very significant performance advance'. Limited deployment starts end-2026, scaling in 2027. Positive for OpenAI's cost curve, a narrative headwind for NVDA a day before earnings.

headline: Marvell jumps 6% as Rosenblatt ($300) and Susquehanna ($265) raise targets on Google warrant deal
summary: Marvell rose 6.7% in morning trade to ~$243, reversing Monday's 4.7% drop, after Rosenblatt initiated at Buy with a $300 target and Susquehanna lifted its target to $265 from $230, following Wells Fargo's move to $310. Analysts cite Alphabet's warrant for ~59M shares tied to roughly $120B of custom AI product business through 2033 (inference accelerators, storage controllers) and 25%+ sequential optical growth. Fiscal Q2 results land Thursday after the close (Fri ~6:30am AEST).

headline: Nvidia snaps seven-day slide as Raymond James lifts target to $352 on server-CPU growth
summary: Nvidia opened +1.4-1.5% at ~$211.66 after Raymond James raised its price target to $352 from $330, calling the CPU franchise 'strategically important' to Nvidia's ecosystem and forecasting a $201B AI server CPU market by 2030 (44% CAGR); the firm upgraded AMD to Strong Buy in the same note. Consensus for Wednesday's report is ~$92B revenue, with options pricing a ~5.4% move.

headline: Consumer confidence dips to 89.4 as expectations sink, but stocks open higher on falling oil and yields
summary: The Conference Board index fell 0.8 points to 89.4 in August (90.2-90.3 expected); the Expectations Index dropped 5.8 points to 68.2 while Present Situation rose 6.8 to 121.2 as 'jobs plentiful' improved to 27%. Stocks shrugged it off: at 10:15 ET the S&P 500 was +0.2% at 7,670, Nasdaq +0.6%, Dow +0.1%, the 10-year eased to 4.65% and Brent fell 2.5% to $88. PCE lands Wednesday and Warsh speaks at Jackson Hole on Friday.

headline: Jack Ma buys HK$600M+ of Alibaba shares; Joe Tsai adds another 720,000
summary: SCMP (owned by Alibaba) reports founder Jack Ma bought more than HK$600M of Hong Kong shares over consecutive days, signalling 'strong confidence' in the AI plan, and chair Joe Tsai bought another 720,000 shares on Tuesday, after the HK$80B placement at a 3.6% discount. Hong Kong shares rose 1.5% and the ADR is +0.35% at $118.88; BofA kept Buy with a $172 target.

headline: Wolfe raises Netflix target to $95, says engagement data points to stronger second half
summary: Wolfe Research lifted its Netflix target to $95 from $84 (22x 2028 EPS of $4.41, up from 20x), arguing Q2's soft subscriber and engagement numbers were a scheduling issue: Q2 releases' prior seasons generated ~765M viewing hours versus 1.3B for Q3's returning titles. Wolfe expects stronger H2 results and solid 2027 guidance. Shares rose 1.7% to $81.39.

headline: Apple unveils 2nm M6 and quad-die M5 Ultra in new Mac mini and Mac Studio; no September invites yet
summary: Apple surprise-launched a Mac mini from $899 on the M6, described as a 'cutting-edge 2 nm process' chip, and a Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra (36 CPU / 80 GPU cores, 1.2TB/s bandwidth); pre-orders open now, shipping after Sept 22. Apple did not send iPhone 18 event invites today; Gurman still expects them this week for a Sept 9 event. The M6 is the first volume 2nm product from TSMC's biggest customer, supportive for TSM.

headline: Google Cloud launches Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services and Legal with Moody's and Weil
summary: Google Cloud announced industry-specific Gemini Enterprise editions for financial services (automating capital-markets and corporate-banking workflows) and legal, with Moody's supplying ratings and research via an MCP server and law firm Weil partnering, a day after the Verizon deal. Vertical enterprise packaging supports Cloud's +82% growth; shares were flat at $347.24.

headline: Meta up 1% as William Blair sees $100B+ AI-agent opportunity; trial week two turns to Instagram design
summary: Meta rose ~1% to $564.58 after William Blair flagged a $100B+ monetization opportunity in Meta's business AI agents, adding to Monday's report that the Hatch consumer agent launches within weeks. The California youth-addiction trial entered week two with testimony focused on Instagram's design, and analysts note the injunction risk exceeds any fine.

headline: Figure +3% as EDX Markets integrates YLDS as collateral and treasury asset
summary: EDX Markets, the institutional crypto exchange, will accept Figure's SEC-registered yield-bearing stablecoin YLDS as collateral and hold it as a treasury asset; executive chairman Mike Cagney said institutions 'shouldn't have to choose between yield, liquidity and regulatory certainty'. FIGR rose 3.4% to $39.97.

headline: Siemens Energy board weighs EUR 10B+ majority sale of steam-turbine unit; no ad-hoc yet
summary: Bloomberg-sourced reports say Goldman Sachs is preparing an auction of a majority stake in the Transformation of Industry division (steam turbines, generators, compressors; ~EUR 5.7B revenue) at a valuation above EUR 10B, with CVC, EQT, Bain Capital, Brookfield and KKR evaluating bids. The supervisory board met on Aug 25 to deliberate; no ad-hoc release had been published as of ~14:45 UTC (before the Xetra close), and Handelsblatt (via Stock-World) expects a final decision only after the next quarterly report. Shares are +3.2% at EUR 153.43 intraday (~14:45 UTC).

headline: Options price a 5.4% (~$280B) Nvidia earnings move, the smallest implied swing in three years
summary: Reuters/ORATS data show options imply a 5.4% move either way after Wednesday's report, below the 12-quarter average of 7.4% and the 6.5% priced ahead of May; ORATS' Matt Amberson called it 'some complacency' and Susquehanna's Chris Murphy said the era of 10-20% post-earnings jumps 'is kind of over'. Focus is on chip demand, margins and hyperscaler capex guidance. NVDA is indicated +1% pre-market at $210.67 after seven straight declines.

headline: US futures rise ahead of Nvidia as Bessent's Iran 'economic onslaught' stops short of penalties
summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent warned countries to cut Iran ties or lose dollar-system access but imposed no new penalties, so Brent slipped to $91.58 and risk appetite recovered: Dow +0.2%, S&P 500 +0.3%, Nasdaq 100 +0.6% pre-market, STOXX 600 +0.3%. Threatened 50% US tariffs on Canada were deferred several weeks. Jackson Hole starts Thursday with Fed Chair Warsh speaking Friday and July PCE due this week.

headline: SK hynix union rejects wage deal by 25 votes; shares still close +0.4% as both sides return to talks
summary: Of 15,045 votes (93.8% turnout), 50.08% opposed a tentative deal offering a 6.3% raise and a profit-share bonus paid 40% cash/60% shares; members objected to the stock-heavy structure. Management and the union will resume negotiations, with an industry source expecting a swift settlement rather than escalation, and no strike was mentioned. SK hynix closed +0.42% at KRW1,678,000 after an early drop, with the Kospi +0.7%. Read-through for Micron: rival labor friction is a minor supply-side wrinkle, not a demand signal.

headline: Lynx Equity calls Micron's CXMT/Apple selloff an overreaction; MU +1.7% pre-market
summary: Lynx's KC Rajkumar argued the report that Apple may source DRAM/NAND from CXMT and YMTC poses little real threat: CXMT is qualified only for one low-volume Mac model, not iPhones, and its poor LPDDR5X yields make it 'structurally incapable' of supplying Apple at scale, while YMTC is not qualified for any Apple product and allocates newer NAND domestically. Micron is indicated +1.7% at $925.80 after Monday's 5.8% drop.

headline: TSMC Taipei shares rebound 1.05% as Asia chip stocks steady ahead of Nvidia; ADR +0.9% pre-market
summary: Asian markets recovered from Monday's tech selloff with investors 'more selective' on chips into Nvidia's report: TSMC closed +1.05% at NT$2,400 and the TAIEX +0.9% after hitting a two-week low intraday, Nikkei +0.58%, Kospi +0.68%, Hang Seng -0.08%, Shanghai +0.19%. TSM ADRs are indicated +0.9% at $413.80 after falling 2.1% on Aug 24.

headline: Alibaba Hong Kong shares +1.5% to HK$114.20 in second day of stabilization, but ADR -1.25% pre-market
summary: After Monday's ~10% drop on the HK$80B ($10.2B) placement to fund AI, 9988.HK rose 1.5% to HK$114.20 at Tuesday's close, helped by the chairman and CEO buying HK$120M of shares. The US ADR is nonetheless indicated -1.25% at $116.99, so the stock has not yet built a base.

headline: Meta to launch 'Hatch' consumer AI agent within weeks, 'Watermelon' model targeted for October
summary: The Information, citing internal documents, reports Meta will release Hatch, the consumer version of its OpenClaw AI agent, as soon as the next several weeks and is targeting October for its next model, Watermelon; Meta has considered tiered pricing for the agent as part of Zuckerberg's push to monetize AI beyond advertising. META is +0.6% pre-market at $562.25 as the California teen-addiction trial enters its second week focused on Instagram's design.

headline: Siemens Energy +1.8% as supervisory board deliberates Goldman-run steam-turbine stake sale; no decision published yet
summary: Shares rose to EUR 151.45 (day range 150.46-152.20) after Bloomberg reported Goldman Sachs has been hired to sell a stake in the steam-turbine unit. German press says the supervisory board is meeting today on the multi-billion-euro division sale and broader separation, but no ad-hoc announcement or press release had appeared on the company's IR or press pages as of 08:45 UTC. Consensus target ~EUR 197; next results Nov 11.

headline: SK hynix reverses 4.5% morning drop to close +0.4% in Seoul; Kospi swings from -4% to +0.7%; Needham lifts ADR target to $220
summary: After the union narrowly rejected the tentative wage deal (60% of bonuses in treasury shares), SK hynix fell to KRW 1,594,500 intraday but closed at KRW 1,678,000 as the KRW 40T buyback and domestic buying absorbed foreign selling; the Kospi closed at 6,742.73. Needham raised its SKHY target to $220 from $200, and the ADR is +2.3% pre-market at ~$159 after a 4.9% drop to $155.37 on Aug 24. Management and the union return to the bargaining table.

headline: Bloom Energy +5% pre-market after Nancy Pelosi discloses first-ever Bloom purchase
summary: A congressional filing shows Pelosi bought roughly $3-4.25M of Bloom Energy stock and options (up to $13.5M combined with Intel), her first Bloom trade, and retail traders bid the stock to ~$214.70 pre-market from a $204.02 close. Coverage ties the buy to the AI power boom; a class action (lead-plaintiff deadline Sep 28) remains a background risk.

headline: Asia rebounds into Nvidia: Kospi +0.7%, Nikkei +0.5%, ASX +0.7%, Taiex +0.9%, Hang Seng flat; Europe and US futures higher as Iran sanction threats fizzle
summary: Nvidia closed -2.9% at $208.48 (seventh straight drop) but is +1% pre-market; options imply a ~$280B swing on Wednesday's print, where consensus looks for ~$92B revenue and ~$104-105B Q3 guidance. July PCE lands the same day (core was 3.3% YoY in June; Fed minutes kept a hike alive) and Chair Warsh gives his first Jackson Hole speech Friday with the 10-year near 4.7%. Brent slipped ~2% to ~$92 as markets shrugged off new US sanctions on Iran. Keyence closed +1.7% at JPY 82,250 and CATL -2.7% at HK$621 with no company news.

headline: Nikkei exclusive: TSMC supplier Nichias to build plant in Taiwan for critical chipmaking 'tubes'
summary: Japan's Nichias, with Gold Stone Development, will build a Taiwan plant for special plastic components used in chip fabrication to avoid the supply disruptions that hampered TSMC's expansions in recent years; a small supply-chain localization step. TSMC shares slipped 0.4% to NT$2,365 in early Tuesday trade as the Taiex opened lower.
